correctness.rationale: Expansion gives two auto-chirp lines b=2ca,2da and cross Gauss sums G(ψ(U)+ηψ(V)); off-line phase difference Δ=−(b−2ca)(b−2da)/(2(c−d)). Because the linear (a,b)->(u,v) map is invertible, each nonzero Δ occurs q−1 times. Trace-zero nonzero elements count q/p−1 and each nonzero trace counts q/p, determining all four ambiguity sectors. For η=−1 (q≡3 mod4), and s>1, trace-zero off-line cells vanish with multiplicity (q−1)(q/p−1); η=1 or q=p gives no zeros. The Weyl directions form an orthonormal HS basis; symplectic Fourier diagonalization gives singular values sqrt(q)|A_g(a,b)| and exact kernel. Cauchy–Schwarz fixes the largest, and discrete cosine/sine traces the smallest, including the p=3 boundary. Independent full ambiguity sums over GF3, GF5, GF7 and GF27 (irreducible polynomial x³+2x+1) reproduced zero counts 0,0,0,208 and q=27 rank521. Finite tests confirm selected cases, all-field proof uses trace and Gauss sums.
residual_risks: Complex-linear matrix-lift noninjectivity in singular cases does not prove nonlinear phase retrieval fails; the theorem properly avoids that inference.
